candidates.summary: harnessSeedsCur's hardcoded frame index is exercised from one of installInheritedCur's two call sites; nothing drives the exemption through the defer path
candidates.failure_scenario: installInheritedCur is called from doOpCall (op_call.go:404) and from doOpReturnCallDefers (op_call.go:841), and its own header says the two paths exist precisely because the defer copy once drifted from doOpCall. harnessSeedsCur reads m.PeekCallFrame(2) with the comment `1 is the callee frame being installed`, which holds on the defer path only because PushFrameCall runs before the block is populated; on that path frame 2 is the frame running its defers, not the frame that made the call. TestHarnessSeedsCur builds two synthetic frames by hand and no test enters the exemption through a deferred crossing call, so a future reordering of doOpReturnCallDefers (pushing the frame after the parameter loop, say) moves the index silently and the test stays green.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'installInheritedCur' gnovm/pkg/gnolang/op_call.go gives two call sites; grep -rn 'harnessSeedsCur' gnovm/pkg/gnolang/*_test.go gives only TestHarnessSeedsCur, which never runs a deferred call. A gno-level test would be a `defer target(cur)` inside a t.Run sub-test in gnovm/tests/stdlibs/testing/.
candidates.evidence: op_call.go:404 `m.installInheritedCur(fr, fv, b)` and op_call.go:841 `m.installInheritedCur(m.LastFrame(), fv, b)`; op_call.go:795 `m.PushFrameCall(&dfr.Source.Call, fv, recv, true)` is what makes index 2 the deferring frame. op_call_test.go:82-110 builds Frames literally.

candidates.summary: the range guard keeps the `n.Op != DEFINE` carve-out that fix 1 removed from the assign guard, and it can never change the outcome
candidates.failure_scenario: Fix 1's premise is that a DEFINE can be a rebind, so the assign guard at 3011 now runs for every op. The range guard at 3100 still skips DEFINE. It cannot matter: RangeStmt's TRANS_BLOCK calls pushInitBlock before defining the key and value, so a range DEFINE always declares in the RangeStmt's own block and isCrossingCurParam returns false for it regardless. One rule now reads two ways across two sites, and the next reader has to redo the block-push argument to see that the surviving carve-out is not a second hole of the kind fix 1 closed.
candidates.verify_by: Delete the `if n.Op != DEFINE {` wrapper at preprocess.go:3100 and run go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles$' -short: no new failure, since `for cur := range xs` inside a crossing function defines in the RangeStmt block.
candidates.evidence: preprocess.go RangeStmt TRANS_BLOCK: `pushInitBlock(n, &last, &stack)` precedes every `last.Define(kn, ...)` for the DEFINE arm; preprocess.go:3011 has no op guard.
